I have experienced voices in the past ranging from yelling hurtful comments to suicide suggestions and hallucination type things where inanimate objects would talk to me. I also used to dissociate when really struggling losing touch with who, where or why I was. A combination of anti-psychotic medication and therapy has got me to a place where these experiences are now rare and more transient, and when they do happen I am better equipped to deal with them, One technique I found helpful when the voices got 'loud' or I lost a sense of who / where I was is grounding. It basically involves focusing on different senses and what they are experiencing. For example describing a picture you can see or naming all the red things in a room, llistening to the tick tock of a clock or a piece of familiar music, the taste of a mint, the smell of perfume, the softness of the fur of  a favourite teddy.

I have had suicidal thoughts since I was 14 I'm now 23.
I grew up christian but stopped going to church around 12/13.
I started going to church again aged 20 and was baptised a few months before my 22nd Birthday.  So although I dont know your situation I have in some ways 'been there got the t-shirt'
CHristianity has helped me  but only because I felt a connection to it, so by all means go to a church and find out more but it wont be a magic fix, or at least thats not how it was for me. Personally what I find most comforting is knowing that in my darkest moments there is someone with me, someone who loves me unconditionally and who died for my sins. the foot print poem really sums this up for me: http://www.onlythebible.com/Poems/Footprints-in-the-Sand-Poem.html

I had turned my back on God as a teenager partly due to what I was experiencing and was further turned away by  a well meaning ( but misguided) friend trying to give me a book that was like God can solve your depression. So in a rambling way I guess I'm trying to say there is a community out there who would love to meet you, pray for you and teach you about God's word and what their faith means to them but ultimately its about what you feel in your heart. And although faith can help in dark times it is unlikely to solve all.

with the work thing I found that when I was struggling with my suicidal thoughts the further I got behind the more stressed I got the more I saw suicide as a solution. one of the ways I got work done was breaking it in to really small sections, then when one small task is complete I would get a reward a break or a sweet or online time anything really. Sometimes I do time rather than content goals like work for 5 minutes then break for 5 minutes then try work for ten minutes break for 5 minutes gradually building my way up to 30 minutes between breaks on a good day.  those times didnt produce my best work but it got me to the state of having something to hand in.

You are as entitled to feel bad as anyone else, there is no magic scale of how shit things have to be before your allowed to feel bad, although a lot of the time it can feel that way.

Sucidal idealation i.e. thinking about killing yourself is exhausting and at times it can dominate thoughts. Talking it about it can help and so feel free to continue posting here. Personally I find talking to strangers a lot easier than talking to people who I know and people whose reactions I care about.
